sections.h2: What does a Susquehanna Township, PA home seller need to know first?
sections.html:
Susquehanna Township is a first-class township on the north side of Harrisburg in Dauphin County, with the ZIP codes 17109 and 17110. Three offices matter: the township for permits, the county treasurer for tax bills, and the Dauphin County recorder for the deed.

The township was carved out of Lower Paxtang Township on May 1, 1815 and takes its name from the Susquehanna River along its western edge. Its first settlement, Coxestown, was laid out in 1757 and later renamed Estherton. The Rockville Bridge, the long stone-arch rail bridge that links the township to Marysville across the river, was added to the National Register in 1975.

sections.h2: How big is the township, and where do its neighborhoods sit?
sections.html:
The township covers 15.3 square miles, of which 13.3 are land and 1.9 are water, and elevations climb from about 300 feet at the river to about 1,150 feet in the northeast on Blue Mountain. That range matters to a seller because a hillside lot and a riverside lot raise very different buyer questions about drainage, access and views.

  • Named communities: Beaufort Farms, Edgemont, Estherton, Lucknow, Montrose Park, Paxtang Manor, Progress and Rockville.
  • Main roads: Interstate 81, U.S. 22, U.S. 322 and Pennsylvania Route 39, plus local arteries such as Elmerton Avenue and Progress Avenue.
  • Neighbors: Middle Paxton and Lower Paxton townships, Swatara Township, Paxtang, Penbrook and Harrisburg, with East Pennsboro Township across the river in Cumberland County.
  • Attractions: the National Civil War Museum sits just inside the boundary, and the Capital Area Greenbelt runs through the township.

sections.h2: How is the housing market in Susquehanna Township put together?
sections.html:
The 2025 Census estimate is 28,434 people, up 6.2 percent from the 26,762 April 2020 base and well past the 24,036 of 2010. No other place in this four-way Census comparison grew as quickly.

Owners live in 62.9 percent of the homes, and the middle owned home was valued at $227,100 in the 2020 to 2024 survey. Rent runs $1,487, above neighboring Swatara, and household income is $84,832. The township has 11,894 households of 2.26 people on average, and 19.9 percent of the population is 65 and over.

Close to 37 percent of homes are rented, so landlords shop alongside owner-occupants. Tell any buyer up front whether the house is occupied and on what lease terms.

sections.h2: What permits and building codes apply to a Susquehanna Township seller?
sections.html:
Residential permits go to the municipal office at 1900 Linglestown Road in Harrisburg, and the township number for questions is 717-909-9251. Every application needs a site plan, and commercial plans go electronically to the Middle Department Inspection Agency.

Pennsylvania adopted the 2021 International Construction Codes effective January 1, 2026, so repairs done after that date follow the newer edition. The township adopted the 2021 International Property Maintenance Code on July 14, 2022, effective July 19, 2022, and that is the standard code enforcement uses on existing houses.

A contractor who disagrees with a ruling can appeal to the Joint Uniform Construction Code Appeals Board. Hearings are held as needed on the fourth Tuesday of each month at 5 p.m. in the Hampden Township Municipal Building in Mechanicsburg.

A public hearing on a Linglestown Road Overlay zoning map and text amendment was scheduled for November 12, 2026. A house along that corridor deserves a call to the township about the final text before you list.

sections.h2: Which office bills property tax in Susquehanna Township, and what transfer tax applies?
sections.html:
Here the Dauphin County Treasurer acts as tax collector, from 101 Market Street, Room 105 in Harrisburg, phone 717-780-6550. Neighboring Swatara Township has its own collector, so the two townships do not share an office.

Dauphin County realty transfer tax split on a Susquehanna Township sale
RecipientShare of priceOn a $227,100 sale
State (Department of Revenue)1.0%$2,271
Municipality0.5%$1,136 (rounded)
School district0.5%$1,136 (rounded)
Total2.0%$4,542

The county Recorder of Deeds supplies that split and keeps deeds dating to 1785. Find it in the courthouse at 101 Market Street, Room 102, phone 717-780-6560. Recording fees can be paid by cash or check, and family transfers are generally exempt.

Ask the treasurer what is owed on your parcel before closing, since the title company deducts any balance from your proceeds.

sections.h2: How does Susquehanna Township compare with its neighbor Swatara?
sections.html:
Susquehanna Township's middle home value of $227,100 runs about $12,700 above Swatara Township's $214,400, and its median household income of $84,832 beats Swatara's $80,444. The two townships touch along the south side, and a buyer shopping the Harrisburg suburbs will often look at both.

The housing mix differs. Swatara has 69.9 percent owner occupancy against 62.9 percent here, and median gross rent is $1,487 in Susquehanna and $1,252 in Swatara. The township also has 1,793 veterans, 12.7 percent foreign-born residents and 90.6 percent of households with a broadband subscription.

These comparisons matter at the negotiating table. If you price against a Swatara sale, remember that the two townships have different rental shares, different school districts and different tax collectors.

sections.h2: How is Susquehanna Township governed, and why does that matter to a seller?
sections.html:
Susquehanna became a first-class township through a Dauphin County Court order on January 2, 1952, and a Board of Commissioners with nine members elected by ward runs it today. Appeals of zoning decisions go to a Zoning Hearing Board, and a separate Township Authority also holds regular meetings.

The township's November 2026 calendar listed meetings of all three bodies, including a Zoning Hearing Board session on November 4, an Authority meeting on November 10 and a Commissioners meeting on November 12. Agendas and minutes are posted in the township's online Agenda Center, so a seller facing a zoning question can read what has already been decided. The township keeps its own police department, which began with a single officer sworn in during September 1955.

sections.h2: Which schools serve Susquehanna Township buyers?
sections.html:
Susquehanna Township School District covers the township with a primary school, an elementary school, a middle school and a high school, and its offices sit on Elmerton Avenue in Harrisburg.

On education, 92.5 percent of adults hold at least a high school diploma and 40.7 percent a bachelor's degree or beyond. A 20.3 minute average commute suits a township beside Harrisburg and along I-81.

sections.h2: What are the practical ways to sell a Susquehanna Township house quickly?
sections.html:
Selling straight to a buyer avoids showings and lets you pick the closing day, while a listing puts the house in front of the most people. Sellers here often face an inherited house, a tenant in place or repairs they would rather skip.

  • Pull your deed copy from the county and request a loan payoff before talking to buyers.
  • Walk the house against the 2021 maintenance code and fix peeling paint, broken steps and loose railings.
  • Write into the offer who pays the 2 percent transfer tax.
  • Compare what a listing would net after fees and repairs with a direct offer, including timing.

Either way the deed is recorded in Harrisburg and the county tax split is the same.

faqs.q: Who bills real estate tax in Susquehanna Township?
faqs.a: The Dauphin County Treasurer, at 101 Market Street, Room 105 in Harrisburg. The treasurer's 2026 collector list shows the county office handling Susquehanna Township, and the phone number is 717-780-6550.

faqs.q: What transfer tax comes with a Susquehanna Township sale?
faqs.a: Two percent of the price: 1 percent to the state and half a percent each to the municipality and school district, according to the Dauphin County Recorder of Deeds.

faqs.q: Where is a Susquehanna Township deed recorded?
faqs.a: Dauphin County. The Recorder of Deeds is in the courthouse at 101 Market Street, Harrisburg, and the office holds deeds back to 1785.

faqs.q: Which building codes does the township follow?
faqs.a: Pennsylvania's Uniform Construction Code governs building work, and the township adopted the 2021 International Property Maintenance Code for existing buildings, effective July 19, 2022. Residential permit questions go to 717-909-9251.

faqs.q: How much has Susquehanna Township grown?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau counted 24,036 residents in 2010 and 26,736 in 2020, and estimated 28,434 on July 1, 2025. That is growth of about 6.2 percent since the 2020 base.
